State vs Sibasish Paul Etc on 5 June, 2024
In The Court Of Ms. Anamika: Mm-06, Ndd, Phc, New Delhi
 State Vs. Sibasish Paul & Anr.

Fir No.: 53/2003

Srl. No. of the case & Date of 39257/2016 dt. 29.04.2003 institution Date of commission of offence 03.02.2003
Name of the complainant Sh. Sunil Kumar Name of the accused 1.Sibasish Paul S/o.
Late S.K. Paul R/o. 630, B-6, Govind Puri, New Delhi.
2.Jitender Kumar Sharma S/o.
Sh. J.L. Sharma R/o. A-133, Sector 19, Noida, UP.

Nature of offence complained of U/s. 304A IPC Plea of the accused person Accused persons pleaded not guilty Date of reserving order 15.02.2024 & 27.04.2024 Final Order Acquitted Date of order 05.06.2024 BRIEF STATEMENT OF REASONS FOR DECISION OF THE CASE:-
1.

In the present case, both accused persons are facing trial for offence punishable under Section 304A IPC on the allegations that on 03.02.2003 at about 6:15 p.m. at subway patri in front of Khadi Gram Udyog within the jurisdiction of PS Connaught Place, accused Jitender Kumar Sharma, being the contractor for electrical and security of subways and accused Sibasish Paul, being the structure engineer of Selvel Media Private Limited, to whom the subways were handed over by NDMC, caused death of one Suraj not amounting to culpable homicide by affixing a wire which was coming from the room of contractor and was having cut in it.
2.
After completion of investigation, charge sheet was filed on 29.04.2003 and copy of charge-sheet was also supplied to the accused persons on the same day.
Notice for offence punishable under Section 304A IPC was given to both accused persons on 15.03.2008 to which they pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
3. To prove its case, the prosecution has examined thirteen witnesses.
4. PW2, PW4, PW7, PW8, PW9, PW11 & PW12 are formal witnesses.
PW2 has proved his dead body State vs Sibasish Paul Etc on 5 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117933791/
1 identification statement Ex.
PW2 / A.
PW4 has deposed that after receiving information that one person has been electrocuted, he informed the PS.
Thereafter, he alongwith ASI Pancham went to RML Hospital where he was left for guarding the dead body in the mortuary of RML Hospital.
PW7 has proved the photographs of the spot Ex. PA to Ex. PJ and its negatives are Ex. PK (collectively).
PW8 has proved the death report Ex. PW8/A and MLC Ex. PW8/B.
PW9 has proved the postmortem report Ex. PW9/A.
PW11 has proved the endorsement on the rukka/tehrir Ex. PW11/A and copy of FIR Ex. PW11/B (OSR).
PW12 has proved his detailed report Ex. PW5/A.
5. PW1 is Raju Gupta @ Topi who deposed that around 6:00- 6:30 p.m., he was present at the market near Rivoli Cinema.
He has further deposed that besides one subway, there was a sign board.
The witness has further deposed that a child was playing on the said sign board who got electric current and his mother cried.
He has further deposed that he rushed to the spot and saw the chld lying down and his body turned blue, thereafter, he was taken to the hospital by the police personnel.
Thereafter, he was cross-examined and discharged on 08.08.2011.
6. PW3 is Meena who has deposed that she used to sell bags near Khadi Gram Udyog, Regal Building, CP, New Delhi.
She has further deposed that on 03.02.2003 at about 4:45-5:00 p.m., she was present at her stall and showing bags to the customers and her son Suraj aged about three and half years was taking food.
She has further deposed that she asked her son to get a side as she was showing the bags to the customer.
She has further deposed that he went towards the subway near which one electrical wire was passing, which was not insulated from something.
She has further deposed that he somehow touched the portion of the wire and was electrocuted and got stuck with the wire.
She has further deposed that she immediately rushed towards him.
She further deposed that when she tried to rescue her child Suraj, she also felt the electric shock.
She has further deposed that her other son Sunil also arrived there and got the hand of Suraj detached from the wire with the help of one danda.
She has further deposed that in the meanwhile, some police official also arrived and took her son to RML Hospital in PCR van.
She has further deposed that she also accompanied them to the hospital.

She has further deposed that after 10 minutes of their reaching the hospital,
the doctors declared her son dead.
She has proved the statement of her son Sunil Ex.
PW3 / A.
She has further deposed that on 04.02.2003, they came to our stall after performing last rites of her son where accused Jitender alongwith one more person came and met her.

Thereafter, he was cross- examined (nil) and discharged on 10.01.2013.
7.

PW5 Sh. Arun Aggarwal, Deputy Electrical Inspector, Labour Department, GNCT, Delhi who has deposed that 11.02.2003, he was posted as Electrical Overseer at Office of Electrical Inspector, 5 Sham Nath Marg, Delhi.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: He has further deposed that on that day on the directions of Electrical Inspector Sh. K.L. Grover, he alongwith Gurpreet Singh Walia, Electrical Overseer went to PS Connaught Place on the request of officials of PS CP for inspection of the site.
He has further deposed that SI Ayub Khan was not available at the PS on that day and they came back.

He has further deposed that after some days, Mr. Ayub Khan made a telephonic call to their office and on 12.03.2003, he alongwith Gurpreet Singh Walia went to the spot near sub-way, Rivoli Cinema,
Connaught Place for inspection alongwith police officials.

He has further deposed that upon State vs Sibasish Paul Etc on 5 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117933791/
2 inspection, they found a sign board of Met Life India Insurance fixed with angle iron on the rear end wall of the entry to the said subway.

He has further deposed that HC Ram Kishan informed that the electrical wires installed for feeding electricity to the said board were removed by the police after the incident and the same were lying in the malkhana of PS CP.
Thereafter, they went to the Malkhana of PS CP where some PVC insulated wires were produced.

They inspected the wires and found certain joints in the wires which were covered with PVC insulation tapes, however, the PVC insulation of the green wire was found damaged at many places and copper conductor of the wire was found exposed at many places.
He has further deposed that the green wire was found blackened with copper conductor exposed at a distance of 1.5 meters from one end which was suggestive of sparking due to short circuit.

He has further deposed that apparently, the live copper conductor came in contact with angle iron which got electrically charged and the child happened to come in contact with the electrically charged angle iron and received the electrical shock.

He has further deposed that upon inspection, they came to conclusion that the electricity supply lines installed to feed the sign board had not been constructed, installed, protected, worked and maintained in such a manner so as to ensure the safety of human being, animals and property which resulted into the said accident.
He has proved the detailed joint inspection report Ex. PW5/A.
Thereafter, he was cross-examined and discharged on 23.10.2013.
8. PW6 Sh. Gurpreet Singh Walia, Deputy Electrical Inspector, Delhi Labour Welfare Board, GNCT has also deposed on the same lines as deposed by PW5.
Thereafter, he was cross- examined and discharged on 17.09.2015.

9. PW10 SI Pancham Singh who has deposed that on 03.02.2003, he alongwith SI Ayub Khan reached at subway near Regal building, they came to know that one child has been electrocuted and has been shifted to RML Hospital by PCR van.

He has further deposed that he alongwith Ct.
Inderjeet went to RML Hospital where child was declared brought dead by the doctors vide separate MLC.
He has further deposed that he obtained the copy of the MLC and shifted the dead body of the child to the mortuary of RML Hospital.
He has further deposed that he came back and handed over the copy of MLC to SI Ayub Khan who got the spot photographed and got the FIR registered.
He has further deposed that SI Ayub Khan took into possession the electric wire from the spot which has various cuts on it vide seizure memo Ex. PW10/A.
He has further deposed that on 07.03.2003, SI Auub Khan formally arrested accused Jitender Kumar Sharma and Sibashish Paul vide arrest memos Ex. PW10/B and Ex. PW10/C respectively.
He has further deposed that the electric wires were also seized on 03.02.2003 by SI Ayub Khan.
He has correctly identified 10 photographs of the electric wires Ex. PA to Ex. PJ.
He has also correctly identified the case property i.e. seized wire wrapped in a white polythene Ex. P2.
Thereafter, he was cross-examined and discharged on 16.12.2026.
10. PW13 is Retd.

SI Ayub Khan IO of the case has deposed that on 03.02.2003, he received a DD No.52B dt. 03.02.2003 upon which I alongwith ASI Pancham Singh went to the spot i.e. Subway, in front of Regal Cinema, Connaught Place.
He has further deposed that they came to know that the injured person/child had been taken to the hospital by PCR van.
He has further deposed that he sent ASI Pancham to the hospital.
He has further deposed that on inquiry, he found the brother and mother of the victim present at the spot.

He inquired from the brother of the victim and recorded his State vs Sibasish Paul Etc on 5 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117933791/
3 statement Ex. PW3/A.
He has further deposed that SI Pancham Singh came at the spot and handed over to him MLC of the deceased and copy of FIR.
He has further deposed that he took into possession the electric wire from the spot which has various cuts on it, photographed the same and seized vide seizure memo Ex. PW10/A.

He has further deposed that on 07.03.2003, he arrested accused Jitender Kumar Sharma and Sibashish Paul vide arrest memos Ex. PW10/B and Ex.
PW10/C.
He has correctly identified the accused Sibashish before court.

He proved the site plan Ex.
PW13/A, 10 photographs of the spot and of wire Ex. PA to Ex. PJ and negatives of the photographs Ex. P3.
Thereafter, he was cross- examined and discharged on 17.09.2022.
11. As no other witness was sought to be examined by the prosecution, PE was closed vide order dated 04.05.2023.
12. Separate statement of both accused persons were recorded U/Sec. 313 Cr.P.C. on 18.05.2023 wherein they denied the case of the prosecution and pleaded innocence.
However, they declined to lead any defence evidence.
13. Final arguments were advanced by Ld. APP for the State and Ld. counsel for accused.
14. I have considered the submissions and perused the record carefully.
15. This being a criminal case, the burden of proving guilt of accused lies upon the prosecution for which the standard required is beyond reasonable doubt.
The accused persons in the present case have been charged with offence punishable under Section 304A IPC.
The said provision deals with the death caused by negligence and consists of two components.
The first is that death should be caused of the victim and the second is that the said death should be caused out of rash or negligent act not amounting to culpable homicide.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case titled as Ambalal D.
Bhatt Vs. State of Gujarat (1972) 3 SCC 525 has held as follows:-
"8.

entities.text:
Ambalal D.
Bhatt Vs. State of Gujarat (1972) 3 SCC 525
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It appears to us that in a prosecution for an offence under Section 304A, the mere fact that an accused contravenes certain rules or regulations in the doing of an act which causes death of another, does not establish that the death was the result of a rash or negligent act or that any such act was the proximate and efficient cause of the death.

If that were so, the acquittal of the appellant for contravention of the provisions of the Act and the Rules would itself have been an answer and we would have then examined to what extent additional evidence of his acquittal would have to be allowed, but since that is not the criteria, we have to determine whether the appellant's act in giving only one batch number to all the four lots manufactured on 12-11-62 in preparing batch No. 211105 was the cause of deaths and whether those deaths were a direct consequence of the appellants' act, that is, whether the appellant's act is the direct result of a rash and negligent act and that act was the proximate and efficient cause without the intervention of another's negligence.

As observed by Sir Lawrence Jenkins in Emperor v. Omkar Rampratap (1902) 4 Bom LR 679 the act causing the deaths "must be the cause causans; It is not enough that it may have been the causa sine qua non".

entities.text: Emperor v. Omkar Rampratap (1902) 4 Bom LR 679
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This view has been adopted by this Court in State vs Sibasish Paul Etc on 5 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117933791/
4 several decisions.

entities.text: State vs Sibasish Paul Etc on 5 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In Kurban Hussein Moham-medali Rangwala v. State of Maharashtra, the accused who had manufactured wet paints without a licence was acquitted of the charge under Section 304A because it was held that the mere fact that he allowed the burners to be used in the same room in which varnish and turpentine were stored, even though it would be a negligent act, would not be enough to make the accused responsible for the fire which broke out.

entities.text: Kurban Hussein Moham-medali Rangwala v. State of Maharashtra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The cause of the fire was not merely the presence of the burners within the room in which varnish and turpentine were stored though this circumstance was indirectly responsible for the fire which broke out, but was also due to the overflowing of froth out of the barrels.
In Suieman Rahiman Mulani v. State of Maharashtra the accused who was driving a car only with a learner's licence without a trainer by his side, had injured a person.

entities.text: Suieman Rahiman Mulani v. State of Maharashtra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was held that that by itself was not sufficient to warrant a conviction under Section 304A.
It would

be different if it can be established as in the case of Bhalchandra v. State of Maharashtra that deaths and injuries caused by the contravention of a prohibition in respect of the substances which are highly dangerous as in the case of explosives in a cracker factory which are considered to be of a highly hazardous and dangerous nature having sensitive composition where even friction or percussion could cause an explosion
, that contravention would be the causa causans."
Hence, it was held that the alleged rash and negligent act should have very close proximity with the factum of death suffered by the victim without the intervention of any third party.
The death should have been the direct result of the rash and negligent act of the accused and the act must be proximate and efficient cause without the intervention of anyone else's negligence.

Hence, it is a settled proposition of law that it is not sufficient to show that the death in question was caused due to any act of the accused but it also needs to be established that the said act was the immediate or proximate cause of the resultant death.
16.
In the present case, PW1 is the independent eye-witness who deposed that the victim was electrocuted while he was playing on the sign board.
However, in his cross-examination, he has stated that he did not see the child/victim climbing or sitting on the sign board.
Further, perusal of the photographs of the concerned sign board Ex. P1 (colly) shows that there is no place for a child to play on the said board.
Hence, it is not clear as to what was the manner in which the victim came into contact with the live wire allegedly running through the sign board.

PW3 i.e. the mother of the victim is another eye-witness examined by the prosecution who has also not deposed regarding the manner in which the victim touched the live wire causing him to receive electric shock.
She has deposed that "he somehow touched the portion of the wire, which was not insulated and was electrocuted and got stuck with he wire."
From the said testimony a sufficient doubt has been raised pointing out towards the contributory negligence on the part of the victim and his guardian who was present at the spot.
It is also not clear whether the electrocution occurred due to the manipulation of the wire by the child or whether it was uninsulated on the date of the accident.
17. Regarding the examination of the wires in question that were supposed to be installed on the advertisement board, the prosecution has examined PW5, PW6 and PW12.
PW5 has deposed that on 11.02.2003, he alongwith PW6 went to PS CP upon instructions of the Electrical Inspector i.e. PW12.

State vs Sibasish Paul Etc on 5 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117933791/
5
On that day, the IO was not available and inspection of the wires was finally conducted on 12.03.2003.
Both PW5 & PW6 have deposed on the same lines and have opined that there was sparking due to short circuit as live copper conductor in the wire came in contact with the iron angle of the sign board.
It was also observed that the PVC insulation upon the wire was damaged in various places.

It is pertinent to note that the incident in question occurred on 03.02.2003 while the inspection and examination of the wires was conducted on 12.03.2003 which is more than one month after the incident.
This creates a doubt regarding the condition of the wires in question at the time of the incident as objects in general are susceptible to general wear and tear due to passage of time.
The prosecution has not been able to prove beyond reasonable doubt as to whether the wires in question had not been properly insulated at the time of incident itself.
PW13 who is the IO has deposed that he took the wires in possession from the spot and clicked photographs of the same.
However, perusal of the said photographs show that they are not close enough to reveal whether the PVC insulation was not present at multiple places upon the wire.
The safe custody of the electric wires after their seizure from the spot has also not been sufficiently proved.

18. It has been argued on behalf of the prosecution that the death of the victim due to electrocution itself reveals that the wires on the advertisement on the Metlife Insurance installed at the spot were not properly insulated.
In this regard, reference has been made to the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur.
However, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in case titled as Syad Akbar vs. State of Karnataka 1979 Cri LJ 1374 has held that the aforesaid doctrine would not apply to a criminal case in the strict sense.

entities.text: Syad Akbar vs. State of Karnataka 1979 Cri LJ 1374
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The following observations were made in this regard.

"Such simplified and pragmatic application of the notion of res ipsa loquitur, as a part of the general mode of inferring a fact in issue from another circumstantial fact,
is subject to all the principles, the satisfaction of which is essential before an accused can be convicted on the basis of circumstantial evidence alone.

Those are: Firstly, all the circumstances, including the objective circumstances constituting the accident,
from which the inference of guilt is to be drawn, must be firmly established.
Secondly, those circumstances must be of a determinative tendency pointing unerringly towards the guilt of the accused.
Thirdly, the circumstances should make a chain so complete that they cannot reasonably raise any other hypothesis save that of the accused's guilt.

That is to say, they should be incompatible with his innocence,
and inferentially exclude all reasonable doubt about his guilt."

Hence, in order to apply the doctrine of res ipsa loquitur, it is essential to demonstrate a complete chain of circumstances beginning from the commission of the negligent act by the accused to the resulting death.
The prosecution in the present case has alleged that both the accused persons were responsible for the safe keeping or maintenance of the wires installed in the sign board at the spot.
Both the eye-witnesses PW1 & PW3 have not deposed regarding the culpability or responsibility of the accused persons.
Hence, it was the duty of the investigating agency to find out as to who was the person responsible for the safe keeping of the premises where the incident occurred.

It has been submitted on behalf of the prosecution that accused Jitender Kumar was the contractor for the electricity supply of the subway (premises in question) and accused Sibashish Paul was the structure Engineer of Selvel Media Pvt. Ltd. to whom the subways were handed over by the NDMC.

State vs Sibasish Paul Etc on 5 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117933791/
6 19.

entities.text: State vs Sibasish Paul Etc on 5 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: From the perusal of the entire record, it is not clear as to what led to the inference that it was the accused persons who were responsible for regular safe keeping of the premises.
The IO PW13 in his cross-examination stated that he has no idea whether any inspection was done by the NDMC prior to the incident.
This leads to a conclusion that no investigation was conducted regarding the role of NDMC in the safe keeping of the electrical wires present at the spot.

The IO has further stated in his cross-examination that he did not collect any document regarding the maintenance of the subway and also did not collect any document to show that any of the accused was the contractor of the electrical work at the premises.
There is no document to show the date on which any contract was given to the accused Jitender Kumar regarding the electrical supply to the subway.
Further, there is no document to show the exact role of the contractor or the structure engineer in maintaining the electrical wires due to which the incident occurred.

Even if it is assumed for a moment that the accused persons were infact responsible for installing the wires in question, there is no documentary or oral evidence to show that both the accused persons were directly responsible for regular inspection of the aforesaid wires or were directly responsible in case of any untoward incident.
Hence, the chain of events required to prove the offence punishable under Section 304A IPC has not been established by the prosecution.

20. In view of the above discussion, this court is therefore, of the view that the prosecution has failed to establish its case beyond reasonable doubt, benefit of which must accrue to the accused persons.
Accordingly, both accused persons namely Sibashish Paul and Jitender Kumar Sharma are acquitted of the offence punishable under Section 304A IPC.
